commits.edited_message:
[subset] Address VARC review findings

Cap the retained component axis values at HB_VAR_COMPOSITE_MAX_AXES.
A VarComponent can declare more axis indices than the coordinate
setter supports, but only the first HB_VAR_COMPOSITE_MAX_AXES values
are consumable; skip the rest instead of growing the axis-values
vector to hold them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

[VARC] Clamp component axis coordinates (#6274)

Axis-value variation deltas can push a rounded component coordinate
outside the range of int. Assigning that float to coord_setter then
triggers undefined behavior in the conversion.

Use hb_clamp_to<int>() after rounding, preserving in-range behavior
while saturating extreme values. Index the axis-values backing store
directly; decompile_record() sizes the vector to match the axis
indices, so the per-element bounds check is redundant here. Add the
minimized raster-fuzzer input.

Tested with meson test -C build and the ASan/UBSan raster fuzzer.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling:
The defect is a length-invariant violation that spans the two edited commits and is present in neither alone.

Commit 801bf6a caps the component axis VALUES retained in the scratch axis_values vector at HB_VAR_COMPOSITE_MAX_AXES (4096) and skips the rest, so after it axisValues.length == min(axis_count, 4096) while the companion axis_indices vector still holds all axis_count entries (a VarComponent may declare up to 8192). Read on its own this is correct, benign hardening: the only consumer then indexed axisValues through the bounds-guarded hb_vector_t::operator[], which yields a safe Crap object for out-of-range indices, so a short axis_values could never be over-read.

Commit 9912fcf later switches the consumer loop in VarComponent::get_path_at to read the vector's raw backing store axisValues.arrayZ[i] instead of the guarded operator[], iterating i over axisIndices.length. Its rationale -- decompile_record() sizes axis_values to match the axis indices -- holds only without the earlier cap. Read on its own (no cap) axisValues.length == axis_count == axisIndices.length, so the raw indexing stays in-bounds and the change is a benign micro-optimization.

Only the composition is unsafe: the first commit leaves axis_values shorter than axis_indices (length 4096, capacity 4602) while the second reads arrayZ[i] for i up to axisIndices.length (8192), running off the end of the 18408-byte heap buffer for i >= 4602 (heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 4).

Neither edited diff contains the bug; each reviewed in isolation is locally correct maintenance, and the defect is unreachable from either single edited commit (base, base+A', and base+B' never overflow; only base+A'+B' fires). A correct fix must reason across the seam -- bound the consumer loop by axisValues.length, or cap axis_indices to match the retained values -- which cannot be derived from either diff alone.
